questions.question: Which command creates reports/2026/q1 even if reports and reports/2026 do not exist yet?
questions.explanation: mkdir -p creates any missing parent directories and does not complain if the path already exists. Plain mkdir fails when a parent is missing.

questions.question: A directory contains jan.csv, feb.csv and mar.csv. What does `echo *.log` print?
options: *.log, because Bash passes an unmatched pattern through unchanged
questions.explanation: By default, when a glob matches nothing Bash leaves the pattern as literal text, so echo prints *.log.

questions.question: Why is `rm -rf $DIR/` dangerous in a script?
options: -f makes rm slower on large directories
If DIR is empty or unset, it expands to rm -rf / and tries to delete everything
rm cannot delete directories, so it always fails
The trailing slash makes rm move files to the Recycle Bin
questions.explanation: An empty variable leaves just /, and -rf removes recursively without prompting. Always check the target and prefer explicit paths.

questions.question: You run `rm current`, where current is a symbolic link to /var/www/payroll/releases/v42. What is deleted?
options: The v42 directory and everything in it
Nothing, because rm refuses to touch symlinks
Both the link and its target
Only the symlink; the target directory is untouched
questions.explanation: A symlink is a separate small file that points at a path. Removing it removes only the pointer, which is why symlink-based deployments can switch or roll back safely.
